href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L3668"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Agent.conversation_parts

``` python
def conversation_parts(
    sid:NoneType=None
):
```

*A stored conversation as ordered, editable parts, rebuilt from the turn
log.*

A branch is another version of the conversation for the model to
continue from, made without changing the recorded history.
`conversation_parts` lists a stored conversation as parts a person can
keep, drop or rewrite: each prompt and reply is editable prose, and each
tool call and result is fixed. It is built from the turn log, not from a
checkpoint. A conversation that someone wants to reshape is usually one
they just resumed, and a resumed session holds no checkpoints.

``` python
shaper = demo_agent()
shaper.ask('In one word, what colour is a clear sky?')
[(p['part_id'].split(':')[-1], p['kind'], p['editable']) for p in shaper.conversation_parts()]
```

``` python
shaper = demo_agent()
shaper.ask('In one word, what colour is a clear sky?')
parts = shaper.conversation_parts()
test_eq([p['kind'] for p in parts], ['user', 'assistant'])
assert all(p['part_id'] and p['turn_id'] and p['group'] for p in parts)
assert all(p['editable'] for p in parts)
test_eq([p['part_id'] for p in shaper.conversation_parts()], [p['part_id'] for p in parts])
```

### Agent.reshape

``` python

    sid:NoneType=None, manifest:NoneType=None, rewrites:NoneType=None, branch_id:str='', revision:NoneType=None
):
```

*Make a reshaped conversation the active branch. The recorded history
does not change.*

Branches can also start from a checkpoint held in this process.
`compile_context` gives a checkpoint’s messages up to a part, keeping or
dropping each group as a manifest of `keep`, `discard` or `auto` says.
`fork` makes those messages the active branch. `undo_turn` is a fork
from before a turn, and `revise` is a fork from after it with the reply
replaced by the person’s text. `switch_branch` makes another branch
active by rebuilding its messages from its parent point. The recorded
turn log never changes.

### Agent.oneshot_stream

``` python
def oneshot_stream(
    prompt, sp:str='', job:str='oneshot', max_tokens:NoneType=None,
    fits:NoneType=None, # `fits(backend)`; a route it refuses ends the search with nothing yielded and is not set aside
    prepare:NoneType=None, # `prepare(prompt, sp, backend)` returns the text for each route; a raised refusal stops the search
    deadline:NoneType=None, # seconds the whole call may take, routing, `prepare` and fitting included
):
```

*The text of `oneshot`’s reply as the model sends it, one chunk at a
time. The next route is tried only while no text has come: a route that
fails or says nothing is set aside, and one that has spoken is never
followed by another. A timeout, a cancel, a failure after text and a
budget stop are raised. Closing the iterator closes the model’s stream.
A route that cannot stream raises
[`StreamUnsupported`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/runtime.html#streamunsupported),
and one that cannot hold a `deadline` raises
[`DeadlineUnsupported`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/runtime.html#deadlineunsupported),
before it is asked. Different backends can run in parallel. Budgets are
soft spend caps, not billing ceilings. Parallel calls can overshoot by
the calls already in flight.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L3852"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Agent.oneshot

``` python
def oneshot(
    prompt, sp:str='', job:str='oneshot', max_tokens:NoneType=None,
    fits:NoneType=None, # `fits(backend)`; a route it refuses ends the search with '' and is not set aside
    prepare:NoneType=None, # `prepare(prompt, sp, backend)` returns the text for each route; a raised refusal stops the search
    deadline:NoneType=None, # seconds the whole call may take, routing, `prepare` and fitting included
):
```

*A question on whichever model `job` routes to, in a conversation that
is thrown away. A cloud model that fails or answers nothing is set
aside, and the question goes to `job`’s next route. Past `deadline` it
raises
[`OneshotTimeout`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/runtime.html#oneshottimeout)
and tries no other route. `prepare` is not interrupted: the deadline is
checked when it returns. A route that cannot hold a `deadline` raises
[`DeadlineUnsupported`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/runtime.html#deadlineunsupported)
before it is asked.*

`oneshot` asks one question that needs no history and no tools, in a
conversation that is thrown away. It runs on the model the `oneshot` job
routes to, or on the `job` you name. A quick question never spends the
turn model’s window. `oneshot_stream` yields text chunks before the
reply is complete. Different backends run in parallel. Each call
captures its usage before releasing its backend lock. The running totals
are updated under a short accounting lock. Budgets are soft spend caps,
not billing ceilings. Parallel calls can overshoot by the calls already
in flight. When a cloud model fails or answers nothing, it is set aside
and the question moves to the job’s next route.

``` python
asker = demo_agent()
said = asker.oneshot('Reply with exactly the word: yes')
said
```

``` python
assert 'yes' in said.lower(), said
test_eq(len(asker.history), 0)
class _Unavailable:
    def _be_or_none(self, job): return None
test_eq(Agent.oneshot(_Unavailable(), 'anything at all'), '')
```

### Agent.summarise

``` python
def summarise(
    text, sp:str='Summarise concisely. Output only the summary.'
):
```

*Summarise `text` on the `summary` job’s model, in a throwaway
conversation.*

`classify` picks one label for a text on the `classify` job’s model, and
[`summarise`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#summarise)
summarises a text on the `summary` job’s model. Both are `oneshot`
calls. Neither adds to the session’s history.

``` python
summariser = demo_agent()
shorter = summariser.summarise('The user asked about thresholds. The agent read pkg/sizes.py and answered 4096.')
shorter
```

``` python
assert len(shorter) < 600, len(shorter)
```

Compaction shortens the conversation when it nears the model’s window.
The summary model writes a summary of the history so far, and the
conversation continues from the summary. With `compact=True` the agent
compacts on its own when the compactor says it is due or the next
message would not fit. Without `compact=`, the agent reads
`compaction.auto` from config.toml, and the default is True.
[`compact()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/learned.html#compact)
does it now, and `extra` tells the summariser what to keep.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L3995"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

```

### Agent.compact

``` python
def compact(
    extra:str='', fresh:bool=False, # summarise everything and keep no recent messages, as `handoff` does
):
```

*Compact the conversation now. Returns the summary text, or `''` with
`compactor.note` set.*

`handoff` is compaction that keeps nothing recent. The summary model
summarises the whole conversation, and the conversation goes on from
that summary alone. The summary’s Done list is kept as a project memory
note. A turn starts a handoff by itself when the conversation is past
the compactor’s soft line and the last turn ended at a boundary: it
completed, and it made a commit or left no unfinished plan step. Past
the hard line, ordinary compaction runs instead. `/handoff` starts one
by hand.

``` python
hb, _ = fake_agent()
hb.history = [dict(state='complete', activity=[])]
assert hb._at_boundary(), 'a clean turn with no plan is a boundary'
hb.plan.add('write the docs')
assert not hb._at_boundary(), 'an unfinished step is not'
hb.history = [dict(state='complete', activity=[dict(tool='git_commit', ok=True)])]
assert hb._at_boundary(), 'a commit closes the work, whatever the plan says'
hb.history = [dict(state='failed', activity=[dict(tool='git_commit', ok=True)])]
assert not hb._at_boundary(), 'a turn that failed never is'
```

### Agent.pct_full

``` python

`problems` collects what went wrong and had nowhere to be reported:
backend failures, a compaction that could not run, a saved approval rule
file that could not be read. It gathers them from every backend. A model
that failed to load is reported whichever job it was routed to. The
property returns the last ten. `pct_full` and `context_used` report how
full the turn model’s window is.

```

assert 0 < asked.pct_full < 1, asked.pct_full

*Everything a status bar or an `/agent` command wants, in one dict.*

`/commit` and `/pr` are the two git flows a session repeats. `commit`
takes the staged diff, or every changed tracked file when nothing is
staged. It drafts a message on the `oneshot` model when none is given,
asks for approval, and commits through `git_commit`. `pull_request`
takes the commits ahead of the default branch, drafts a title, asks for
approval, pushes the branch when it has no upstream, and opens the pull
request on GitHub. When GitHub is out of reach, it prints the
`gh pr create` command to run instead. Both work on the repository
holding `path`, by default the project’s.

```

*Run a slash command. Returns text to show, or None when the command is

This cell replaces `ask` and `stream` with the versions every frontend
uses. Each turn is now a registered run, an object with an id and a
state that can be watched and cancelled, and a stopped turn is still
recorded. `ask` takes three more options, for a host that runs agent
jobs:

- `schema`, a pydantic type or a JSON schema dict. The model gets a
  `submit_result` tool and is asked to hand back a value of that type,
  once more if it does not. The validated value arrives in
  `TurnResult.result`.
- `result=True` returns a
  [`TurnResult`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#turnresult):
  the reply, the turn’s state (`complete`, `failed`, `cancelled`,
  `budget` or `abandoned`), its usage and its ids.
- `strict=True` raises
  [`TurnFailed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#turnfailed)
  for a turn that did not complete, and
  [`ResultMissing`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#resultmissing)
  when the schema was never filled.

`queue` holds a prompt for after the current turn, and `run_queued` runs
the held prompts in order. `cancel(run_id)` stops one run, or the
foreground turn, and returns its final state. `terminate` stops it
without waiting for the provider. A turn in a session another process
holds raises
[`SessionBusy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#sessionbusy).
The budgets `max_cost`, `max_tokens` and their `session_` forms stop a
turn that passes them, and the turn is recorded with state `budget`.

### SessionBusy

``` python
def SessionBusy(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*A turn in a session another live process holds.*

A run’s transcript is a plain text file under `runs_dir`. Anything that
can tail a file can follow a sub-agent or a folder review.

- `watch(target)` opens a tmux pane following a run’s transcript, or
  `monitors` for the folder reviews, coloured in the palette of the
  terminal session’s `now.json` beside it (`setup.follow_cmd`). With no
  target it lists what can be watched. Without tmux it prints that
  command to run instead.
- `tell(run_id, text)` queues a message for a running sub-agent, which
  reads it after its next tool call.
- `steer(text)` does the same for the main turn. This is called
  steering. The text arrives with the turn’s next tool result, tagged
  with the session’s `inbox_key`. The briefing explains the tag to the
  model. The terminal steers when you press enter mid-turn.
- `leftovers` returns, once, what the main turn was sent and never read.
  The next turn starts with it.

`expand_command` turns a `/name ARGS` line into the prompt it stands
for. A skill name stays as it is. A markdown file in `<cfg>/commands/`,
or in a root’s `.agents/commands/` when `project_extensions` is on, has
`$ARGUMENTS` and `$1..$n` filled in and each `@path` replaced by the
file’s text.

``` python
from ramabana.testing import ScriptedBackend, Step

steered, _ = fake_agent()
sbe = ScriptedBackend(steps=[Step('looking'), Step(tool=('view_file', {'path': '/proj/a.py'})), Step('done')], token_delay=0, tools=steered.tools)
steered._be = steered._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': sbe
test_eq(steered.steer('idle'), '')
g = steered.stream('go'); next(g)
assert steered.steer('check the tests too')
list(g)
tag = f'<user-message key="{steered.inbox_key}">\ncheck the tests too\n</user-message>'
assert next(m['content'] for m in sbe.hist_ if m['role'] == 'tool').endswith(tag)
assert inbox_note(steered.inbox_key) in steered.system_prompt() and steered.run().key == steered.inbox_key
test_eq(steered.leftovers(), [])

sbe.steps = [Step('an answer in two words')]
g = steered.stream('again'); next(g)
steered.steer('one more thing'); list(g)
test_eq(steered.leftovers(), ['one more thing'])
test_eq(steered.leftovers(), [])
```

Every turn leaves a row in the log with a `state`, however it ended. A
resume gives back `complete` and `failed` turns whole (`REPLAYED`), and
a row written before `state` existed counts as `complete`. A `cancelled`
turn comes back too. The person stopped it, and the next turn builds on
its prompt, its partial reply and what was sent during it. Its reply
ends with a note that the turn was interrupted. The fragment never reads
as a whole answer. An `interrupted` turn, one whose process ended
mid-turn, comes back with a similar note. An `abandoned` turn, a stream
nobody finished reading, does not come back. A `budget` turn does not
come back either.

``` python
import json

def _rows(a):
    "What survives a restart, which is the file rather than `a.history`."
    p = a.history_path
    return [json.loads(l) for l in p.read_text().splitlines()] if p and p.exists() else []

dropped = demo_agent()
g = dropped.stream('a question nobody waited for')
chunk = next(g)
g.close()

rows = _rows(dropped)
test_eq(len(rows), 1)
test_eq(rows[0]['state'], 'abandoned')
test_eq(rows[0]['reply'], chunk)
test_eq(dropped.busy, False)
```

``` python
kept = demo_agent()
list(kept.stream('a turn that finished'))
row = kept.history[-1]

def replayed(state):
    kept.history = [dict(row, state=state, prompt=f'a {state} turn')]
    kept.resume_session(kept.session_id)
    b = kept._be('turn')
    return ' '.join(m.get('content', '') for m in (b._resume_hist or b.hist or []))

for state in REPLAYED: assert f'a {state} turn' in replayed(state), state
said = replayed('cancelled')                     # the user stopped it, and the next turn builds on it
assert 'a cancelled turn' in said and 'interrupted' in said
assert 'a abandoned turn' not in replayed('abandoned')   # a dropped stream is a fragment, not a turn

kept.history = [{k: v for k, v in row.items() if k != 'state'}]
kept.resume_session(kept.session_id)
b = kept._be('turn')
assert 'a turn that finished' in ' '.join(m.get('content', '') for m in (b._resume_hist or b.hist or []))
```

`set_model(name, job)` points a job at another model. Changing the turn
model carries the live conversation to the new model, and rebuilds the
tools when the new model’s budget or profile differs. An unknown name
raises.

``` python
routed = demo_agent()
routed.set_model('gpt-4.1', 'subagent')
routed.spec_or_none('subagent')
```

routed = demo_agent()
before = routed.model
routed.set_model('gpt-4.1', 'subagent')
test_eq(routed.spec_or_none('subagent').model_id, 'openai/gpt-4.1')
test_eq(routed.model, before)
test_fail(lambda: routed.set_model('no-such-model'))
```

`subagent_writes` says whether sub-agents get write tools. An
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) turns
it on by default, and the sub-agents’ writes still go through this
session’s approvals. The terminal’s `--no-subagent-writes` and
`/subagents off` turn it off. `demo_agent` turns it off too, and it
reads False here. `set_subagent_writes` changes it while no turn is
running.

``` python
writer = demo_agent()
writer.subagent_writes
```

``` python
test_eq(writer.subagent_writes, False)
writer.set_subagent_writes(True)
test_eq(writer.subagent_writes, True)
writer.set_subagent_writes(False)
test_eq(writer.subagent_writes, False)
```

compacted = demo_agent()

compacted = demo_agent()

before = len(compacted.history)
compacted.compact()

### Pictures the model sent back, and pictures its tools drew

A model that generates images returns them on the response, not in its
text. They arrive as `media` on the assistant’s history message, and
`resp_media` collects them after the turn; streaming yields only text.

A tool result is text, so a tool that draws writes a file and returns
its path. `on_media` is called with the paths as soon as the tool writes
them, so a frontend can show the picture while the turn runs.
`last_media` gives both kinds as `{'mime', 'data'}` dicts holding the
bytes, for a frontend that cannot open a path.

[`fake_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fake_agent)
from [testing](04_testing.ipynb) is a real
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) whose
every job routes to one scripted backend that returns the replies you
give it, so a turn runs here with no model at all.

``` python
agent, be = fake_agent(host, replies=['`threshold` is in `ramabana/runtime.py`.'])
agent.ask('where is the compaction threshold?')
```

``` python
agent, be = fake_agent(host, replies=['no pictures here'])
agent.ask('hello')
test_eq(agent.last_media, [])

be.chat.hist.append({'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'here you go', 'media': [{'mime': 'image/png', 'data': b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nx'}]})
test_eq([m['mime'] for m in agent.last_media], ['image/png'])
first, _ = fake_agent(host); second, _ = fake_agent(host)
assert first.session_id != second.session_id
```

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    shot = Path(d)/'shot.png'
    shot.write_bytes(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nx')
    drawer, _ = fake_agent(host, replies=['drawn'])
    seen = []
    drawer.on_media = seen.append
    drawer._drew([shot])
    test_eq(seen, [[shot]])
    test_eq(drawer.resp_media, [])
    test_eq([m['mime'] for m in drawer.last_media], ['image/png'])
```

Each turn records its plan in `_turn_plan`: whether the person named
tools (`explicit`) or the model chooses (`model`), and which tools and
skills were named. No tool was named in `hello`, so the model chose.

``` python
agent._turn_plan
```

With no tool named, nothing runs ahead of the model. The message the
backend received is the prompt as typed.

``` python
print(be.sent[0][-400:])
```

`calls` and `turn_lines` show what the turn ran. The scripted reply
called no tool, so both are empty.

``` python
agent.calls, agent.turn_lines()
```

`status()` on the fake agent after its turn, showing a few of its keys:

``` python
{k: v for k, v in agent.status().items() if k in ('ready', 'busy', 'model', 'ntools', 'pct_full', 'usage')}
```

`changes()` compares files, not what a tool said about them. Here
`create_file` writes `/proj/b.py`, and `changes()` reports it with an
empty before-text. A tool that claimed success and changed nothing would
not appear.

``` python
agent.ask('create a file')
create = next(t for t in agent.tools if t.__name__ == 'create_file')
create('/proj/b.py', 'def b(): return 2\n')
agent.changes()
```

A shell command’s changes are measured the moment it returns, not when
the turn ends. The agent reads the open folders before the command and
compares them right after. A file that someone else changes later in the
turn is not credited to the command. `changes()` feeds `/rewind` and the
host’s journal, and a comparison at the end of the turn would offer to
revert somebody else’s work. In the example the command changes `a.py`,
then `elsewhere.py` changes outside it, and only `a.py` is reported.

``` python
shell_host = MemHost({'/proj/a.py': 'a = 1\n', '/proj/elsewhere.py': 'e = 1\n'})
shell_agent, _ = fake_agent(shell_host)
shell_agent.before.clear()
run_shell = next(t for t in shell_agent.tools if t.__name__ == 'run_shell')

def _ran(command, cwd=None, timeout=120):
    shell_host.files['/proj/a.py'] = 'a = 2\n'
    return 0, 'done'

shell_host.run_cmd = _ran
run_shell('touch a.py')
shell_host.files['/proj/elsewhere.py'] = 'e = 2\n'
test_eq(shell_agent.changes(), {'/proj/a.py': ('a = 1\n', 'a = 2\n')})
```

Slash commands are methods of the agent, not of a frontend. Every
frontend offers the same set. `command` returns None for an unknown
command. The frontend then passes the line on.

``` python
agent.command('/tools').splitlines()[:4]
```

``` python
test_eq(agent.command('/nope'), None)
print(agent.command('/model'))
```

The short jobs run away from the turn model, each in a conversation that
is thrown away. With
[`fake_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fake_agent)
every job goes to the scripted backend, which answers `ONESHOT:`
followed by the question.

``` python
agent.oneshot('is this a question?'), agent.summarise('a long transcript')
```

``` python
agent.compact(), agent.compactor.note
```

Most problems happen on the short jobs, such as a compaction that could
not run or a completion the engine refused, where the caller has no
exception to catch. That is why the agent collects them in `problems`.

``` python
agent.problems, agent.pct_full, agent.context_used
```

## Inline completion

Inline completion suggests the next few lines of code at the cursor, as
an editor does. It returns at most four lines. It has to feel instant,
and each call is worth little. It runs on the `completion` job’s model
in a throwaway conversation. It runs only when asked for, never on every
keystroke. The kernel’s own completions are instant and correct, and
this costs a model call.

[`_clean`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#_clean)
makes a raw reply safe to insert. Asked for bare code, a completion
model often wraps it in a fence, repeats the line it continues, and
writes past the point where it can guess.
[`_clean`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#_clean)
takes the code out of the fence, drops the repeated text, and keeps at
most `max_lines` lines.

``` python
before = 'def threshold(ctx, reserve=RESERVE):\n    '
_clean('```\n    if not ctx: return None\n    return max(1, ctx - reserve)\n```', before, 4)
```

``` python
test_eq(_clean('    ' + 'x = 1', '    ', 4), 'x = 1')
_clean('a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf', '', 3)
```

A small local model can write prose and then a fence that the token
limit cut off before it closed. Everything before the fence is prose,
and inserting it would be worse than suggesting nothing.
[`_clean`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#_clean)
keeps only the code after the fence.

``` python
reply = 'Looking at the code, `area(r)` returns nothing. Let me fix it:\n```python\n    return math.pi * r**2'
_clean(reply, before, 4)
```

``` python
test_eq(_clean('I will explain first.\n```python', before, 4), '')
_clean('```\ncomplete block\n```', '', 4)
```

any related code, the kernel’s variables and the project’s memory in the

comp.ready, comp.complete('def a():\n    ', 12)

`max_tool_calls` and `max_steps` are per-turn budgets. `auto` leaves a
budget uncapped by the agent.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>budget</th>
<th>range</th>
<th>caps</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>max_tool_calls</code></td>
<td>20 to 400</td>
<td>tool calls in a turn</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>max_steps</code></td>
<td>8 to 80</td>
<td>model calls in a turn</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A value outside the range is clamped to it. A call past the tool budget
returns a message telling the model to stop and summarise.
`/tool-budget` and `/steps` change the budgets mid-session.

The step budget reads two private attributes of urai’s chat:
[`_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#_steps) and
`_budget_exceeded`.
[`_steps_over`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#_steps_over)
reports a step stop when `_budget_exceeded` is set and
[`_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#_steps) has
reached `max_steps`. urai also sets `_budget_exceeded` to recover a full
window, so a turn that recovers its window after exactly `max_steps`
steps is recorded as a step stop. Ramabana accepts this limit.
`test_urai_leaves_the_state_the_step_cap_reads` fails when a urai
release changes either attribute.

`runs(active=True)` lists what is running, each run with its live
children. A finished sub-agent is left out, unless a sub-agent it
started is still running.

``` python
from ramabana.testing import fake_agent
from ramabana.runtime import Run

a, be = fake_agent(replies=['done'])
root = a._new_run('parent'); root.start(be)
done = Run('child_done', kind='child', parent=root)
going = Run('child_going', kind='child', parent=root)
done.start(be); done.finish(); going.start(be)
test_eq([c['id'] for c in a.runs(active=True)[0]['children']], ['child_going'])
test_eq(len(a.runs()[0]['children']), 2)
deep = Run('grandchild', kind='child', parent=done); deep.start(be)
kids = {c['id']: c for c in a.runs(active=True)[0]['children']}
test_eq(sorted(kids), ['child_done', 'child_going'])
test_eq([c['id'] for c in kids['child_done']['children']], ['grandchild'])
```

Once a run is cancelled, any tool call it attempts is not started, and
returns a note saying so.

Cancelling a streamed turn stops it at once. The stream ends with what
had arrived, the run leaves the active list, and the turn is recorded
with state `cancelled`. The turn is not finished. No check runs, and no
checkpoint is saved. `on_registered` is called with the run before any
output. A host can keep the run id. A cancel there means the model is
never called.

``` python
from ramabana.testing import FakeBackend, fake_agent

class _BlockingBackend(FakeBackend):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(replies=['unused'])
        self.first, self.release, self.cancelled = threading.Event(), threading.Event(), False
    def stream(self, msg, run=None, **kw):
        yield 'partial'; self.first.set(); self.release.wait(); yield 'late'
    def cancel(self): self.cancelled = True; self.release.set(); return True

a, _ = fake_agent(replies=['unused'])
be = _BlockingBackend()
a._be = lambda job='turn': be
a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': be
a.cancel_grace = .05
finished, remembered, chunks = [], [], []
a._finish = lambda *args, **kw: finished.append(args)
a._remember = lambda *args, **kw: remembered.append((args, kw))
t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: chunks.extend(a.stream('stop me')), daemon=True)
t.start(); assert be.first.wait(.2)
run_id = a.status()['runs'][0]['id']
result = a.cancel(run_id); t.join(.2)
test_eq(result['state'], 'cancelled')
test_eq(chunks, ['partial'])
test_eq((finished, a.status()['runs']), ([], []))
test_eq(len(remembered), 1)
test_eq(remembered[0][0][:1], ('stop me',))
test_eq(remembered[0][1], {'state': 'cancelled'})

class _SnapshotBackend(FakeBackend):
    def _stream(self, msg, **kw): yield from ('The ', 'The answer', 'The answer')

a, _ = fake_agent(replies=['unused'])
be = _SnapshotBackend()
a._be = a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': be
test_eq(list(a.stream('repeat')), ['The ', 'answer'])
test_eq(a.history[-1]['reply'], 'The answer')

a, _ = fake_agent(replies=['unused'])
be = _BlockingBackend()
a._be = a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': be
registered, chunks = [], []
def registered_before_output(run):
    registered.append(run.id)
    run.cancel(0)
test_eq(list(a.stream('register first', on_registered=registered_before_output)), [])
test_eq((len(registered), be.first.is_set()), (1, False))

a, _ = fake_agent(replies=['unused'])
be = _BlockingBackend()
a._be = a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': be
def registration_failed(run): raise RuntimeError('registration failed')
test_eq(list(a.stream('bad registration', on_registered=registration_failed)),
        ['\n\nthe assistant failed (RuntimeError: registration failed)'])
test_eq(a.runs(active=True), [])
test_eq(be.first.is_set(), False)
```

`cancel` stops the turn in flight and reports the run it stopped.
Nothing is running here, so the report is an idle run with no children.

``` python
asked.cancel()
```

``` python
test_eq(asked.cancel(), {'id': None, 'state': 'idle', 'children': []})
test_eq(asked.busy, False)
```

`close` ends the session. It closes watch panes, background delegations
and the approval gate, cancels active runs, closes every backend and the
host, and releases the session lock. A closed agent reports `ready`
False.

``` python
asked.close()
asked.ready
```

``` python
asked.close()
test_eq(asked.ready, False)
asked.close()
```

``` python
a, be = fake_agent(replies=['done'])
order = []
be.cancel = lambda: order.append('cancel') or True
be.close = lambda: order.append('close')
a._backends[('fake', 'fake/model')] = be
run = a._new_run('shutdown'); run.start(be)
a.close()
test_eq(order[:2], ['cancel', 'close'])
```

``` python
prompt = '''<notebook path=a.ipynb>
...
</notebook>

<user-request>
why is it reading a.ipynb and df_norm
</user-request>

<tool-plan route="direct">Answer directly.</tool-plan>
<system-reminder>Verify it.</system-reminder>'''
test_eq(request_text(prompt), 'why is it reading a.ipynb and df_norm')
test_eq(request_text('plain request'), 'plain request')
test_eq(request_text('<user-request></user-request>'), '')
```

``` python
class _BusyAgent:
    runs = Agent.runs
    busy = Agent.busy

for state in ('pending', 'running', 'cancelling'):
    a = _BusyAgent()
    root = Run('root', state=state)
    a._runs, a._runs_lock, a._foreground = {'root': root}, threading.RLock(), 'root'
    assert a.busy

for state in ('completed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'detached', 'terminated'):
    a = _BusyAgent()
    root = Run('root', state=state)
    a._runs, a._runs_lock, a._foreground = {'root': root}, threading.RLock(), 'root'
    assert not a.busy

a = _BusyAgent()
root = Run('root', state='completed')
root.child('delegated').state = 'running'
a._runs, a._runs_lock, a._foreground = {'root': root}, threading.RLock(), 'root'
assert a.busy
root.children[0].finish()
assert not a.busy
```

The history log is one JSONL file shared by every session with the same
`history_name`, and a long-lived one reaches tens of megabytes. This
cell replaces the simple history methods with indexed ones.
`rebuild_index` reads the log once and records, for each session, its
turn count, title, first and last byte offsets and model, in
`<history_name>-sessions.json`. Each new turn is added to the index as
it is written. `sessions` and `session_turns` read from the index, and
`sessions` first writes an `interrupted` row for any turn whose process
died (`recover_turns`).

`set_title` and `summarize_session` set a session’s title, the second by
asking the summary model. `set_muted` marks a session as muted.
`branches` and `save_branch` keep the branch records in
`<history_name>-branches.json`. One lock per log file keeps two agents
in one process from interleaving their writes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L5224"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

`compact_history(cfg)` rewrites a log written before pictures were
logged as `[image]` and before long results went to the details file. It
holds the lock
[`_append_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#_append_line)
takes for the whole pass, streams the log into a temporary file beside
it, and replaces the log in one rename. A row with nothing to change
keeps its bytes. In the others, a picture’s bytes become `[image]`, and
each result over `RESUME_DETAIL` goes whole to its session’s details
file, in the shape `_slim` writes, unless that file holds its id
already; the row keeps the start of the result. The session index is
rebuilt afterwards and keeps its titles, mute flags and folders. A
writer that queued on the old file notices the replacement and appends
to the new one.

Another live process holding a session stops the pass, unless `force` is
set, and a writer that does not finish within `wait` seconds does too.
The old log and index stay as `.pre-compact` files unless
`backup=False`. `ramabana history compact` runs it. A row `_slim` leaves
over `ROW_MAX` also sends its prompt to the details file, and
[`hydrate_turns`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/history_core.html#hydrate_turns)
puts it back.

``` python
cdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
cold = {'at': 1.0, 'session': 's1', 'turn_id': 't1', 'state': 'complete', 'model': 'm', 'reply': 'ok',
        'prompt': str([b'\x89PNG' * 5000, 'what is this?']),
        'activity': [{'id': 'a1', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'x' * 5000}]}
(cdir/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(cold) + '\n')
cgot = compact_history(cdir, backup=False)
cgot
```

The log is a fraction of its size, and the session reads back as it did:
the prompt in its `[image]` form, the result whole.

``` python
cag, _ = fake_agent(cfg=cdir)
cturn = cag.session_turns('s1')[0]
test_eq(cgot['after'] < cgot['before'] / 10, True)
test_eq(len(cturn['activity'][0]['detail']), 5000)
turn_prompt(cturn)
```

A picture `generate_image` saves to a `path` is recorded like any write,
so `/rewind` deletes a picture the turn created.

``` python
def generate_image(prompt: str, path: str = '') -> str: return path or 'media/generated-1.png'
ga, _ = fake_agent()
draw = ga._record(generate_image)
draw('x'); test_eq(ga.before, {})
draw('x', path='/proj/new.png'); assert '/proj/new.png' in ga.new and '/proj/new.png' in ga.before
```

A tool’s `read_only` copy is recorded too. A read-only view, such as a
read-only sub-agent or plan mode, is given that copy, and its calls
reach the activity feed and the history like any other.

``` python
from shalya import read_only as _read_only
def read_url(url: str, remember: bool = True) -> str: return f'read {url}'
def _no_save(url: str) -> str: return read_url(url, False)
_no_save.__name__ = 'read_url'; read_url.read_only = _no_save
def generate_image(prompt: str, path: str = '') -> str: return path or 'media/generated-1.png'
def _draw_only(prompt: str) -> str: return generate_image(prompt)
_draw_only.__name__ = 'generate_image'; generate_image.read_only = _draw_only
ra, _ = fake_agent()
view = {t.__name__: t for t in _read_only([ra._record(read_url), ra._record(generate_image)])}
view['read_url']('https://x.test'); view['generate_image']('rama')
test_eq([r['tool'] for r in ra.activity.rows()], ['read_url', 'generate_image'])
test_eq(ra.activity.rows()[0]['args'], {'url': 'https://x.test'})
rr = ra._record(read_url); assert ra._record(rr) is rr and rr.read_only._recorded
```

``` python
from shalya import LocalHost
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d, TemporaryDirectory() as c:
    root = Path(d); png = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + bytes(8)
    def generate_image(prompt: str, n: int = 1, path: str = '') -> str:
        for t in write_targets('generate_image', {'path': path, 'n': n}): (root/t).write_bytes(png)
        return 'drawn'
    ga, _ = fake_agent(LocalHost([root], index=False), cfg=Path(c))
    ga._record(generate_image)('x', n=2, path='img.png')
    test_eq(sorted(ga.new), ['img-2.png', 'img.png'])
    ga._checkpoint()
    ga.rewind(ga.current_turn_id, what='files')
    test_eq(sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir()), [])
pv = preview_for('generate_image', {'prompt': 'rama', 'n': 2, 'path': 'img.png'})
assert 'img.png' in pv and 'img-2.png' in pv, pv
test_eq(write_targets('create_file', {'path': 'a.py'}), ['a.py']); test_eq(write_targets('generate_image', {'prompt': 'x'}), [])
test_eq(write_targets('generate_image', {'path': 'a.png', 'n': 'two'}), ['a.png'])

rr = ra._record(read_url)
@functools.wraps(rr)
def other(*a, **kw): return rr(*a, **kw)
assert ra._record(other) is not other and ra._record(rr) is rr
rb, _ = fake_agent(); assert rb._record(rr) is not rr
n0 = len(rb.activity.rows()); rb._record(rr)('https://y.test'); test_eq(len(rb.activity.rows()), n0 + 1)
```

Each tool call is saved in the log with its string arguments whole, up
to `ARG_TEXT` (2,000) characters with newlines kept, so a replay of the
call has the full image prompt or file text. A resumed context still
shows each argument clipped to one short line.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    ha, _ = fake_agent(cfg=Path(d))
    prompt = ('Pahari miniature, Kangra school; ' * 50)[:1499] + '\nno text'
    act = ha.activity.start('generate_image', {'prompt': prompt, 'size': '1024x1536', 'n': 1})
    ha.activity.finish(act, 'media/generated-1.png')
    ha._remember('draw rama', 'drawn')
    row = json.loads(ha.history_path.read_text().splitlines()[-1])
    test_eq(row['activity'][-1]['args'], {'prompt': prompt, 'size': '1024x1536', 'n': 1})
test_eq(_arg('x' * (ARG_TEXT + 5)), 'x' * ARG_TEXT + '…')
resumed = _resumed_acts([{'tool': 'generate_image', 'args': {'prompt': prompt}}])
assert len(resumed) < 700 and '\nno text' not in resumed, resumed
```

Because the log is large, `_load_history` reads only its last
`HISTORY_TAIL` bytes (8 MB) and keeps at most the last `HISTORY_TURNS`
(2,000) turns, whichever gives fewer. The model’s context is rebuilt
from that tail. A session picker needs more, since the conversations
worth offering are mostly older than the tail, so `session_turns` seeks
to the session’s byte range from the index. The range is a filter, not a
list of lines, because two live sessions interleave in one log.

``` python
import json as _json, tempfile as _tf
_cfg = Path(_tf.mkdtemp())
_pad = 'x'*400
_rows = ([{'at':1,'session':'old','prompt':f'ancient {_pad}','reply':'r','model':'gpt-mini'}] +
         [{'at':10+i,'session':'new','prompt':f'{i} {_pad}','reply':'r','model':'gpt-mini'} for i in range(30)])
(_cfg/'tail-history.jsonl').write_text('\n'.join(_json.dumps(r) for r in _rows)+'\n')

_hold, HISTORY_TAIL = HISTORY_TAIL, 2000
_a = Agent(NullHost(['.']), cfg=_cfg, history_name='tail', extensions=False)
test_eq({t['session'] for t in _a.history}, {'new'})
test_eq([s['id'] for s in _a.sessions()], ['new', 'old'])
test_eq(_a.sessions()[1]['turns'], 1)
test_eq(_a.session_turns('old')[0]['prompt'][:7], 'ancient')
HISTORY_TAIL = _hold

# `ensure_ascii=False` writes U+2028 raw, and `str.splitlines` breaks a record there
_sep = [{'at':1,'session':'s','prompt':'a\u2028b','reply':'r','model':'m'}, {'at':2,'session':'s','prompt':'c','reply':'r','model':'m'}]
(_cfg/'sep-history.jsonl').write_text('\n'.join(_json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) for r in _sep)+'\n{broken\n', encoding='utf-8')
_s = Agent(NullHost(['.']), cfg=_cfg, history_name='sep', extensions=False)
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in _s.history], ['a\u2028b', 'c'])
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in _s.session_turns('s')], ['a\u2028b', 'c'])
```

A tool result longer than `RESUME_DETAIL` (600 characters) is written
whole to `<history_name>-details/<session>.jsonl`, before the turn’s
row, and the row keeps its first 600 characters and a `details`
reference. A resume replays only those 600 characters, so the row alone
resumes the session. `session_turns` puts the whole results back, for a
branch editor or a transcript. A row written before this has its results
inline and reads as it always did. `hydrate_turns(cfg, turns)` does the
putting back for any rows read from `<cfg>`’s log, so a reader without
an agent, such as Dhrona, sees whole results too. The session index
lists each session’s byte ranges in `spans`, so `session_turns` reads a
session’s own rows rather than every row between its first turn and its
last. An index row written before `spans`, or one past `MAX_SPANS`
ranges, falls back to that first-to-last range.

``` python
import itertools, json as _json, tempfile as _tf
_dc = Path(_tf.mkdtemp())
da, _ = fake_agent(cfg=_dc)
for out in ('x' * 5000, 'y' * RESUME_DETAIL, 'short'):
    da.activity.finish(da.activity.start('run_shell', {'command': 'ls'}), out)
da._remember('list', 'listed')
row = _json.loads(da.history_path.read_text().splitlines()[-1])
test_eq(row['details'], f'agent-details/{da.session_id}.jsonl')
test_eq([len(a['detail']) <= RESUME_DETAIL + 40 for a in row['activity']], [True] * 3)
test_eq([a['detail'][:1] for a in row['activity']], ['x', 'y', 's'])
test_eq(row['activity'][1]['detail'], 'y' * RESUME_DETAIL)
test_eq(len(_json.loads((_dc/row['details']).read_text())['details']), 1)
test_eq(da.history[-1]['activity'][0]['detail'], _clip('x' * 5000))
whole = da.session_turns(da.session_id)
test_eq(whole[-1]['activity'][0]['detail'], _clip('x' * 5000))
test_eq(_as_messages(whole), _as_messages([da.history[-1]]))
rows = [_json.loads(l) for l in da.history_path.read_text().splitlines()]
test_eq(hydrate_turns(da.history_path.parent, rows)[-1]['activity'][0]['detail'], _clip('x' * 5000))
with open(_dc/row['details'], 'a') as f: f.write('{"turn_id": "t", "deta')
test_eq(da.session_turns(da.session_id)[-1]['activity'][0]['detail'], _clip('x' * 5000))
(_dc/row['details']).rename(_dc/'gone.jsonl')
test_eq(da.session_turns(da.session_id)[-1]['activity'][0]['detail'], row['activity'][0]['detail'])
test_eq(hydrate_turns(_dc, [{'details': '/etc/passwd', 'activity': []}, {'details': '../x/y', 'activity': []}])[0]['activity'], [])
na, _ = fake_agent()
na.activity.finish(na.activity.start('run_shell', {'command': 'ls'}), 'z' * 5000)
test_eq(na._slim({'turn_id': 't', 'activity': na.activity.rows()}), {'turn_id': 't', 'activity': na.activity.rows()})

_sc = Path(_tf.mkdtemp())
_rs = [{'at': i, 'session': s, 'prompt': f'{s}{i}', 'reply': 'r', 'model': 'm'} for i, s in enumerate('aabab')]
(_sc/'sp-history.jsonl').write_text(''.join(_json.dumps(r) + '\n' for r in _rs))
sp = Agent(NullHost(['.']), cfg=_sc, history_name='sp', extensions=False)
ends = list(itertools.accumulate(len(_json.dumps(r)) + 1 for r in _rs))
test_eq(sp.rebuild_index()['a']['spans'], [[0, ends[1]], [ends[2], ends[3]]])
test_eq(sp.rebuild_index()['b']['spans'], [[ends[1], ends[2]], [ends[3], ends[4]]])
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in sp.session_turns('a')], ['a0', 'a1', 'a3'])
with open(sp.history_path, 'a') as f: f.write(_json.dumps({'at': 5, 'session': 'b', 'prompt': 'b5', 'reply': 'r', 'model': 'm'}) + '\n')
test_eq(sp.rebuild_index()['b']['spans'][-1], [ends[3], sp.history_path.stat().st_size])
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in sp.session_turns('b')], ['b2', 'b4', 'b5'])
test_eq(sp.rebuild_index(), sp.rebuild_index(force=True))
_idx = _json.loads(sp.sessions_path.read_text())
for r in _idx['sessions'].values(): r.pop('spans')
sp.sessions_path.write_text(_json.dumps(_idx))
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in sp.session_turns('a')], ['a0', 'a1', 'a3'])
with open(sp.history_path, 'a') as f: f.write(_json.dumps({'at': 6, 'session': 'a', 'prompt': 'a6', 'reply': 'r', 'model': 'm'}) + '\n')
assert 'spans' not in sp.rebuild_index()['a']
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in sp.session_turns('a')], ['a0', 'a1', 'a3', 'a6'])
import ramabana.history_core as _core
_hold, _core.MAX_SPANS = _core.MAX_SPANS, 1   # `_add_span` reads the limit from `history_core`
assert 'spans' not in sp.rebuild_index(force=True)['a']
test_eq([t['prompt'] for t in sp.session_turns('a')], ['a0', 'a1', 'a3', 'a6'])
_core.MAX_SPANS = _hold
_lc = Path(_tf.mkdtemp())
la, _ = fake_agent(cfg=_lc); lb, _ = fake_agent(cfg=_lc)
for x in (la, lb, la): x._remember('hi', 'there')
test_eq(len(la.rebuild_index()[la.session_id]['spans']), 2)
test_eq(len(la.session_turns(la.session_id)), 2)
```

`status()` returns everything a status bar shows, in one dict:
readiness, whether a turn is running, the model and profile, the
budgets, the approval mode, context use, cost, the plan, recent
activity, the waiting approval and the active runs.

``` python
bar = demo_agent()
{k: v for k, v in bar.status().items() if k in ('ready', 'busy', 'model', 'tool_budget')}
```

``` python
st = bar.status()
assert 'claude-sonnet-4-5' in str(st['model'])
```

`/tools` and `/model` on the demo agent. A line that is not a slash
command also returns None.

``` python
bar.command('/tools').splitlines()[:3]
```

test_eq(bar.command('/nope'), None)
test_eq(bar.command('not a command'), None)

`compile_conversation` gives the provider messages for a reshaped
conversation: the stored turns, minus what a person discarded, with
their own words in place of any prose they rewrote. A call and its
result move together, and neither can be rewritten, because editing one
would claim work that never ran.

``` python
shaper.compile_conversation()['messages']
```

``` python
whole = shaper.compile_conversation()['messages']
test_eq([m['role'] for m in whole], ['user', 'assistant'])
pid = shaper.conversation_parts()[-1]['part_id']
test_fail(lambda: shaper.compile_conversation(manifest={pid: False}))
fewer = shaper.compile_conversation(manifest={pid: 'discard'})['messages']
test_eq([m['role'] for m in fewer], ['user'])
mine = shaper.compile_conversation(rewrites={pid: 'Cyan, actually.'})['messages']
assert 'Cyan, actually.' in str(mine[-1])
```

`reshape` makes a reshaped conversation the active branch. The turn log
still records what happened; only the model’s context changes.

``` python
pid = shaper.conversation_parts()[-1]['part_id']
shaper.reshape(rewrites={pid: 'Cyan, actually.'})
```

``` python
logged = len(shaper.history)
pid = shaper.conversation_parts()[-1]['part_id']
br = shaper.reshape(rewrites={pid: 'Cyan, actually.'})
assert br['branch_id'] and br['branch_id'] != 'main'
test_eq(shaper.current_branch_id, br['branch_id'])
test_eq(len(shaper.history), logged)
```

A branch is stored as its parent point plus its manifest, so switching
rebuilds the messages rather than copying them.
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main), the
conversation as recorded, is always there to return to. `/branches`
lists the branches and `/branch NAME` switches.

``` python
shaper.switch_branch('main')
shaper.current_branch_id, [b['branch_id'] for b in shaper.branches()]
```

``` python
shaper.switch_branch('main')
test_eq(shaper.current_branch_id, 'main')
ids = [b['branch_id'] for b in shaper.branches()]
assert 'main' in ids, ids
test_eq(shaper.switch_branch('main')['branch_id'], 'main')
```

## What a read may send

Every tool result goes to the model, and for a hosted model that means
to another company’s servers.
[`mk_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_host)
gives the host a `read_guard` built by
[`masking_guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#masking_guard),
and shalya asks it about every read the tools make: files, notebook
cells, search hits, diffs, web pages, shell output and Python output.
The guard answers with the text to send instead, or a refusal.

Secrets are masked in every read, always, whatever `--pii` says, by
[`mask_secrets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mask_secrets)
(its shapes are listed with the shell rules above). A key is found by
its prefix on a word boundary, so one glued to a word character, such as
`XSK_sk_live_…`, is not; a key with no fixed prefix, such as an AWS
secret access key or a Hetzner token, is never found, and the shell
rules and the file tools’ refusal of credential paths are what keep
those out.

Personal data is masked only where `--pii` asks, which needs `--vault`,
and only in shell, Python, URL and page reads sent to a hosted model,
that is, when `ReadCheck.local` is false or unknown. With `redact` the
guard masks rahasya’s personal-data kinds; with `refuse` it withholds a
read that holds any. Code reads (`view_file`, `view_cell`, `grep`,
diffs) get their secrets masked and nothing else, because the agent
edits files by exact text: an email address masked in a file it reads
would make every `oldText` around it match nothing. A local model sees
personal data as it is. A key masked in a file can still break an edit
whose `oldText` spans it; that edit fails and says so, and is the price
of never sending the key.
[`secret_denial`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#secret_denial)
stops the worse case, a write tool putting `[SECRET]` back over the key;
a shell or Python write such as `sed -i` is not checked.

The guard learns which model reads from the host’s `model_local`, which
[`mk_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_agent)
points at
[`Agent.model_local`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.model_local):
a sub-agent’s model while one runs, else the turn’s.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L5327"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

def masking_guard(
    policy:NoneType=None, # callable -> `(pii, pii_ner)`, asked on each read; None masks secrets only

*A host `read_guard` that masks secrets in every read, and personal data
in the shell, Python and web reads a hosted model gets.*

``` python
from shalya.core import ReadCheck
```

The same printed text, read three ways under `--pii redact`: shell
output to a hosted model loses the key and the address, shell output to
a local model loses only the key, and a file read to a hosted model
loses only the key.

``` python
printed = 'OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test' + 'q' * 30 + '\nmail ada@example.com'
redacting = masking_guard(lambda: ('redact', False))
reads = dict(hosted=ReadCheck('ls', 'run_shell', 'shell', lambda: printed, local=False),
             local=ReadCheck('ls', 'run_shell', 'shell', lambda: printed, local=True),
             code=ReadCheck('/proj/a.py', 'view_file', 'text', lambda: printed, local=False))
sent = {k: redacting(r) for k, r in reads.items()}
sent
```

``` python
test_eq(sent, dict(hosted='OPENAI_API_KEY=[SECRET]\nmail [EMAIL]', local='OPENAI_API_KEY=[SECRET]\nmail ada@example.com',
                  code='OPENAI_API_KEY=[SECRET]\nmail ada@example.com'))
test_eq(masking_guard()(ReadCheck('a.py', 'view_file', 'text', lambda: 'x = 1')), None)
withheld = masking_guard(lambda: ('refuse', False))(reads['hosted'])
withheld
```

## Assembly

[`mk_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_agent)
is the one call that builds a working session: a
[`WorkspaceHost`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/vault.html#workspacehost)
over the named folders, an
[`Approvals`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#approvals)
gate in the mode `approve` names (`none` builds no gate), and an
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) on
both. The terminal and the MCP server start here, and so can any
application that runs agent jobs.
[`mk_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_host)
builds just the host, with the web, vault, API-specification and PII
options, and gives it
[`masking_guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#masking_guard)
as its `read_guard` unless the caller passes one.

Pass `cfg=` for history, skills and saved approval rules, `read_roots=`
for folders to search but never write, `python='off'` to withhold
Python, and any other
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent)
option by keyword. The agent starts without a code index;
[`host_kw`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#host_kw)
controls it. The [index](index.ipynb) shows a session driven from
Python.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L5351"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### mk_agent

``` python
def mk_agent(
    roots:tuple=('.',), model:NoneType=None, approve:str='ask', # ask | edits | auto | off | none (no gate)
    web:bool=True, # wire the web tools to fossick
    vault:bool=False, # keep reads in a vishalakshi vault
    spec:bool=False, # let the agent load OpenAPI/Azure/GCP specs
    read_outside:bool=False, # read-only tools may name any path
    pii:str='off', # off | redact | refuse PII from the vault, and from shell, Python and web reads a hosted model gets
    pii_ner:bool=False, # gate titled names too, not only patterns
    host_kw:NoneType=None, # to `mk_host`: `index` (off: `sync_index` runs it after the model), `warm`, `vault=<path>`
    read_roots:tuple=(), # folders the read tools search and no write touches
    python:str='host', # 'host' runs `run_python` in this process, 'off' withholds it
    rules_path:NoneType=None, # saved allow/deny rules; None shares `<cfg>/approvals.json` with every session on that cfg
    timeout:NoneType=None, # seconds an ask waits for an answer; None waits forever
    no_listener:str='refuse', # an ask with nobody listening: 'refuse', or 'wait' for a listener
    on_timeout:str='refuse', # an ask nobody answers in time: 'refuse' or 'allow'
    **kw
):
```

*A host over `roots` and an
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) on
it, gated as `approve` says; no code index until asked.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/agent.py#L5337"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### mk_host

``` python
def mk_host(
    roots:tuple=('.',), approvals:NoneType=None, # gates writes on this host
    web:bool=True, # wire the web tools to fossick
    vault:bool=False, # keep reads in a vishalakshi vault
    spec:bool=False, # let the agent read and call an API spec
    read_outside:bool=False, # read-only tools may name any path
    pii:str='off', # off | redact | refuse PII from the vault, and from shell, Python and web reads a hosted model gets
    pii_ner:bool=False, # gate titled names too, not only patterns
    **kwargs
):
```

*The workspace host shared by the terminal, MCP and ACP, with secrets
masked in every read unless `read_guard` says otherwise.*
